title: Legislative districts of Dinagat Islands
wikitext:
{{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Dinagat Islands''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Dinagat Islands]] in the [[Congress of the Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the Congress through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Surigao|Legislative district of Surigao del Norte}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Dinagat Islands were initially represented under the former province of [[Surigao (province)|Surigao]] (1907–1961), [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region X]] (1978–1984) and [[Surigao del Norte]] (1961–1972; 1984–2007). The passage of Republic Act No. 9355 on October 2, 2006 and its subsequent [[2006 Dinagat Islands creation plebiscite|ratification by plebiscite]] three months later separated seven municipalities from Surigao del Norte's [[Legislative districts of Surigao del Norte#1987–2007|first congressional district]] to form the new province of [[Dinagat Islands]].{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 9355 - An Act Creating the Province of Dinagat Islands|date=October 2, 2006|access-date=August 9, 2016|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Senate of the Philippines|url=https://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209355.pdf}} The new province first elected its separate representative in the [[2007 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2007 elections]]. Despite Dinagat Islands being nullified as a province by the [[Supreme Court of the Philippines]] on February 11, 2010{{cite news|last1=Rempillo|first1=Jay B.|title=SC Voids Creation of the Province of Dinagat Islands|url=http://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/news/courtnews%20flash/2010/02/02111002.php|access-date=December 19, 2015|publisher=Supreme Court of the Philippines|date=February 11, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716102903/http://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/news/courtnews%20flash/2010/02/02111002.php|archive-date=July 16, 2011}} the decision was not yet rendered final and executory before the [[2010 Philippine House of Representatives elections|May 10, 2010 elections]]; therefore the [[Commission on Elections (Philippines)|Commission on Elections]] still organized the elections for Dinagat Islands' congressional representative along with its provincial officials.{{cite web|author=Commission on Elections|title=COMELEC Resolution No. 8790|url=https://comelec.files.wordpress.com/2010/03/com_res_8790.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100326191935/https://comelec.files.wordpress.com/2010/03/com_res_8790.pdf|archive-date=March 26, 2010|date=March 9, 2010|access-date=August 9, 2016|url-status=dead}} Even after the Supreme Court rendered its original decision final and executory on May 18, 2010, the representatives of the reconfigured [[Legislative districts of Surigao del Norte#1st District|first district of Surigao del Norte]] and the lone district of Dinagat Islands continued to represent their own constituencies.{{cite web|url=http://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/jurisprudence/2011/april2011/180050.htm|date=April 12, 2011|title=G.R. No. 180050, Promulgated: April 12, 2011|publisher=Supreme Court of the Philippines|first=Antonio Eduardo B.|last=Nachura|access-date=August 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819044441/http://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/jurisprudence/2011/april2011/180050.htm|archive-date=August 19, 2016|url-status=dead}} After the Supreme Court reversed its previous ruling on April 12, 2011, and subsequently upheld with finality the constitutionality of R.A. 9355 and the creation of Dinagat Islands as a province through an Entry of Judgment on October 24, 2012,{{cite web|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2013/01/09/ira-shares-for-lgus-jump-by-37-5-in-2013/|title=IRA Shares for LGUs Jump by 37.5% in 2013|date=January 9, 2013|publisher=Office of the President of the Philippines|author=Department of Budget and Management|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|access-date=August 9, 2016}} the separation of Dinagat Islands from Surigao del Norte's first district became permanent. == Lone District == * '''Population (2015)''': 127,152{{cite web|url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx|website=Philippine Statistics Authority|date=2015|title=Population of Population of Legislative Districts by Region, Province, and Selected Highly Urbanized/Component City: 2015|access-date=November 19, 2017}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
